items.comparison: The cadaveric study directly examines both femoral head attachments. It describes the lateral head at the posterior-superior lateral femoral condyle, while the medial head has a thick tendinous region wrapping around the posterior condyle to an anterior-superior attachment. The displayed sentence bundles both heads; the modern comparison therefore qualifies rather than uniformly confirms it. No project-mesh boundary is supplied.
The selected study examines proximal femoral attachments and does not measure the displayed distal shared Achilles/calcaneal insertion. This is not a direct modern comparison for this sentence.

The study's lateral-head dissection describes attachment at the posterior-superior surface of the lateral femoral condyle. It does not define a reproducible boundary on the project's femur mesh or approve a surface annotation.

The study describes a thick medial-head tendinous region wrapping around the posterior medial condyle to an anterior-superior attachment. This is a material detail beyond a simple posterior-superior description; it does not define project-mesh coordinates.

The article measures in-vivo soleus fascicle architecture and uses two cadaveric muscles for corroborating architecture. It does not experimentally measure the displayed tibial/fibular origin footprint.
The article does not measure the displayed shared Achilles-tendon/calcaneal insertion footprint.

The cadaver study directly examines tibial attachment endpoints and reports different levels for anterior and posterior fibers, including sex-related variation. It does not experimentally assess every fascia/septum clause in the displayed sentence and supplies no project-mesh surface boundary.

The paper mentions the medial-cuneiform/first-metatarsal insertion in its discussion of prior descriptions, but its measurements focus on the tibial origin. It does not experimentally measure the displayed distal tendon footprint.
The paper's study is about distal tibialis-posterior tendon footprints. Its proximal origin sentence appears as background and is not a result of this dissection study.

The dissection found a main navicular insertion in 41/41 specimens and variable additional mid/hindfoot footprints. It supports the displayed sentence's main navicular and expanded-insertion context at a broad level; the exact attachment wording and any location on the project's mesh remain unapproved.
The study investigates distal peroneal tendon insertions, not the displayed fibularis-longus origin. Its abstract is not direct support for this sentence.
The abstract reports first-metatarsal insertion in 13 of 20 feet and variants in 7 of 20. It does not verify the displayed first-cuneiform extension, and the full text was not opened.
Both linked studies concern distal tendon insertion, not the displayed fibularis-brevis origin. The KCI full-text PDF and the Foot and Ankle Surgery full text were not opened.

The KCI abstract reports three insertion morphologies among 96 Korean feet and a mean insertion length; it is an abstract-level check. The other abstract reports a fifth-metatarsal insertion in 11 of 20 feet and variants in 9 of 20. Neither abstract defines a boundary on the project's fifth-metatarsal mesh.
